extra_misconceptions.fact: Ultraviolet radiation from an electric arc travels tens of feet and reflects off bright walls, causing painful flash burns.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Looking at a welding arc from across the shop without a shaded lens is safe because distance blocks ultraviolet rays.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Butter traps heat and causes infection, while ice freezes damaged tissue; flush minor burns gently with cool running water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying butter or ice directly to a thermal burn from hot slag cools the damaged skin tissue safely and quickly.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hydrocarbon vapours remain trapped in metal pores and seams, requiring steam purging or inert gas filling before hot work.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rinsing an empty fuel container with water makes the metal drum completely safe to cut or weld with a torch.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Milk does not prevent metal fume fever in the lungs; only source capture ventilation and approved respirators stop inhalation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drinking cold milk after inhaling zinc oxide fumes neutralizes heavy metal toxins inside the digestive and respiratory tracts.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to weld on galvanized steel without local exhaust ventilation or a properly fitted respirator?
What happens to the cornea during arc eye, and why do painful symptoms often appear several hours after exposure?
Where should a Scout position fire extinguishers and a fire watch before striking an arc near combustible shop walls?
Which physical indicator distinguishes heat exhaustion from life-threatening heat stroke inside a hot welding booth?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard sunglasses lack sufficient infrared and ultraviolet filtration, requiring ANSI Z87.1 shaded welding lenses for every arc.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dark polarized sunglasses provide adequate eye protection when tack-welding steel plates together for just a few seconds.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Impact-rated safety glasses with side shields must stay on under the hood to stop hot slag when lifting the helmet to chip.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Safety glasses are unnecessary underneath a full-face welding helmet because the flip-down hood blocks all flying debris.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Molten sparks burn straight through canvas and catch in frayed hems; high-top leather boots with cuffless pants are mandatory.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Frayed cotton jeans and canvas sneakers protect your feet and ankles from molten metal droplets during flat position welding.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A stray spark or radiant heat can puncture a plastic butane lighter, causing a pressurized flame explosion against your leg.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carrying a butane lighter in your front pants pocket is harmless while welding as long as your leather apron covers it.

extra_socratic_questions: Which section of a Safety Data Sheet lists the hazardous decomposition fumes released when an electrode coating burns?
Why is it dangerous to wear synthetic polyester or nylon shirts underneath a leather welding jacket in the shop?
What shade number range on a welding helmet filter lens is required to protect your eyes during GMAW or SMAW?
Under what condition does cuffing your work trousers or leaving shirt pockets unbuttoned create a severe burn hazard?

extra_misconceptions.fact: True fusion welding melts both the base metal edges and the filler metal so they coalesce into a single continuous grain structure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Welding simply glues two pieces of steel together using melted filler wire without melting the base metal edges.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Slag insulates the cooling weld to prevent brittle martensite formation and atmospheric oxidation until the metal cools down.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Slag left on top of a stick weld should be chipped off while glowing red-hot so the underlying steel cools faster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Compressed air contains roughly seventy-eight percent nitrogen and twenty-one percent oxygen, causing severe weld porosity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Compressed shop air from a standard tire compressor can substitute for argon shielding gas to blow smoke away from the arc.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Autogenous welds in processes like GTAW fuse tight-fitting base metal edges directly together using only the heat of the arc.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: All welding processes require adding a separate consumable filler rod or wire to bridge the joint between two metal plates.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the mechanical strength of a steel weld bead if atmospheric nitrogen and oxygen enter the molten pool?
Which physical function does solidified flux slag serve over the hot weld metal immediately after the arc moves forward?
Under what condition does an electrode act strictly as a heat conductor rather than melting to supply filler metal?
What metallurgical difference separates true fusion welding from lower-temperature brazing or soldering on steel joints?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The preheat flame only raises steel to kindling temperature; the pure oxygen jet rapidly oxidizes the iron and blows out slag.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An oxy-acetylene cutting torch severs thick steel plate solely by melting a slot through the metal with its preheat flame.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Aluminum and stainless steel form refractory oxides with melting points higher than the base metal, blocking oxy-fuel oxidation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Oxy-fuel torches cut aluminum and stainless steel just as cleanly as mild carbon steel when fuel pressure is turned up.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Plasma cutters use an electric arc to superheat non-flammable gases like compressed air or nitrogen into an ionized plasma jet.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plasma arc cutters require cylinders of flammable acetylene gas to ionize the cutting stream and slice conductive metals.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mechanical cutting severs metal through cold shear or chip removal, avoiding the thermal distortion and hardening of torch cuts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mechanical shearing and bandsaw cutting leave a wide heat-affected zone that hardens the cut edge of mild steel plate.

extra_socratic_questions: What chemical reaction actually severs carbon steel after the oxy-fuel preheat flames bring the edge to kindling temperature?
Why is it dangerous to cut stainless steel or cast iron using a standard oxy-acetylene cutting torch setup?
What happens to the kerf edge and heat-affected zone when plasma arc cutting is used instead of a mechanical bandsaw?
Which physical indicator on the top edge of a steel plate confirms that preheat flames are ready for the oxygen cutting jet?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Turning the regulator screw counterclockwise relieves spring tension so high cylinder pressure does not slam the diaphragm.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Backing out a regulator adjusting screw until it feels tight increases gas flow into the welding torch hose prior to opening.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Free acetylene becomes chemically unstable above fifteen psi and can decompose explosively even without oxygen present.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Acetylene gas can be safely regulated and used at line pressures above fifteen pounds per square inch for heavy cutting.

extra_misconceptions.fact: SMAW and GTAW require constant-current machines to stabilize amperage, while GMAW and FCAW use constant-voltage power sources.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Constant-current power sources and constant-voltage power sources are interchangeable between stick welding and MIG wire feeders.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rust and paint add electrical resistance that causes erratic arc starting; clamp directly to clean bare metal near the joint.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Clamping the ground cable onto a painted or rusty table leg far from the joint provides a clean electrical return path.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to oil a compressed gas regulator or open an acetylene cylinder valve past one and a half turns?
What measurement on a flowmeter gauge confirms proper shielding gas delivery in cubic feet per hour before GMAW welding?
Where should a Scout position the work clamp on the workpiece to prevent arc blow and poor electrical ground contact?
Under what condition does outdoor wind make Flux-Cored Arc Welding or SMAW superior to gas-shielded GMAW?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excessive weld reinforcement wastes filler metal and creates sharp stress risers along the weld toes without adding strength.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Piling a tall, rounded weld bead high above the plate surface creates a stronger joint than a flat, well-fused bead.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thermal expansion and contraction exert immense force that warps untacked plates; tack welds at both ends hold alignment.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Clamping one end of a butt joint by hand without tack welds keeps the two steel plates aligned during welding.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ink burns off before the arc arrives and carbon from graphite can contaminate sensitive alloys, whereas soapstone stays visible.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Using a graphite pencil or permanent ink marker instead of soapstone is ideal for sketching layout lines on hot steel.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An overly long arc scatters heat, increases spatter, reduces root penetration, and lets atmospheric gases cause weld porosity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Holding a very long arc length helps the molten filler metal spread out wider and penetrate deeper into a fillet joint.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to weld penetration and bead profile when your travel speed across the steel plate is noticeably too fast?
Which physical indicator in the weld toe shows undercut caused by excessive amperage or an improper electrode angle?
Where should a Scout place tack welds on a tee joint or corner joint to prevent thermal distortion during the final pass?
What percentage of lateral overlap between adjacent stringer beads ensures a smooth, flat pad without deep valleys?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Welder performance qualifications apply only to the specific process, position, base metal group, and thickness range tested.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Passing a single welding certification test qualifies a welder to perform every welding process on any metal thickness.

extra_misconceptions.fact: AWS welder certification requires signed continuity verification every six months confirming the welder still uses that process.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An AWS Welding Certification lasts for life without requiring ongoing continuity logs or periodic employer verification.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Welding careers span robotics programming, metallurgical engineering, nondestructive testing, and certified code inspection.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Careers in the welding industry are limited to manual shop floor production work with no pathways into engineering.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The American Welding Society is a nonprofit professional organization that publishes consensus standards and administers exams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The American Welding Society is a federal government agency that issues criminal fines to local metal fabrication shops.

extra_socratic_questions: What practical difference separates an AWS Certified Welder performance test from an AWS Certified Welding Inspector role?
Which non-destructive testing methods allow an inspector to detect internal weld cracks without cutting the finished joint?
Under what condition does an AWS Certified Welder credential expire if the welder stops working with that specific process?
